questions.answer: Plaintiff Reddit, Inc. filed the 2026-09-25 motion (Dkt 144). It moves under Rule 12(b)(6) to dismiss SerpApi's counterclaims. SerpApi's counterclaim (Dkt 119, filed 2026-08-28) pleads Sherman Act s.2 monopolization and attempted monopolization, plus four declaratory counts. It alleges Reddit gave Google exclusive crawl access under a deal reportedly worth about $60M a year, and that a robots.txt from 2024-07-01 blocked other search engines. It seeks treble damages, an injunction against requester-specific robots.txt rules, and a declaration of no DMCA claims before January 2025.

claims.claim: Reddit, Inc. (plaintiff) filed the 2026-09-25 motion (Dkt 144), under Rule 12(b)(6), to dismiss SerpApi LLC's counterclaims.
SerpApi's counterclaim (Dkt 119, filed 2026-08-28) pleads monopolization and attempted monopolization under Sherman Act s.2, with Clayton Act ss.4/16 remedies, plus four declaratory-judgment counts.

The theory is that Reddit gave Google exclusive crawl access, under a partnership reportedly worth about $60M a year. From 2024-07-01 it served other crawlers (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Mojeek, Qwant) a blocking robots.txt. The claimed market is large-scale human conversational data in topic-organized forums, used for search indexing and AI training.
SerpApi seeks treble damages, an injunction against requester-specific robots.txt directives, and a declaration that Reddit has no cognizable DMCA claims before January 2025.

The KB (serpapi.md:78) had inferred Reddit as the filer ('likely Reddit against the counterclaim [inferred]'). Unverifiable: r10 (Reddit blocks fetches). Pages on earlier motions or the July 31 ruling, which don't cover the September motion: r4-r9, r12, r15-r19, r23, r26, r27, r29. Press Gazette (r25) doesn't mention the counterclaim. questions.answer: The case is pending. On 2026-07-20 the court dismissed Google's DMCA claims: without leave to amend for results with no copyrighted content, with leave for results containing copyrighted material. Google filed an amended complaint on 2026-08-10, narrowed to licensed content (Reddit plus two unnamed licensors). SerpApi moved to dismiss it with prejudice on 2026-08-24 (Dkt 49). On 2026-09-15 the court denied SerpApi's bid to get Google's licensing agreements. The hearing date conflicts: ppc.land says 2026-09-29; the KB, from a later docket read, says 2026-10-13.

claims.claim: Google's amended complaint (2026-08-10) narrows the case to licensed content. It pleads licensing agreements with Reddit and two unnamed licensors, and drops the Google Shopping and Maps examples.
SerpApi moved on 2026-08-24 (Dkt 49) to dismiss the amended complaint with prejudice; the motion was pending as of September.
On 2026-09-15 Judge Gonzalez Rogers denied SerpApi's bid to compel production of Google's licensing agreements.
The 2026-07-20 order dismissed Google's original DMCA claims: without leave to amend for results with no copyrighted content, with leave to amend for results with a copyrighted component.

questions.notes: The docket pages (r13 CourtListener, r25 Justia) returned 403 or a Cloudflare challenge, so the hearing date couldn't be re-checked. ppc.land (r23, 2026-08-25) quotes the notice of motion's 2026-09-29 date. The KB says the hearing is 2026-10-13 and the reply is due 2026-09-29, per a 2026-09-04 schedule, so r23 is likely stale. crawlraven (r11) dates the second motion 2026-08-25, not 2026-08-24. The Bloomberg Government piece (r15) is paywalled past the ruling. r14 and r18 are copies of the order itself. r20 is SerpApi's amicus brief in the D.C. Circuit U.S. v. Google appeal (2026-08-04), not this case. Filing-era or background pages: r2, r5, r8, r17, r26, r28. Unverifiable: r4 (Jenner, 403). r22 (Reddit) was not fetched.
